prompt: What does Retrofit write for you from the `PlannerApi` interface?

choices.text: The server that answers the requests
choices.why: Retrofit is a client; the server is somebody else's, or MockWebServer in tests.

choices.text: The code that builds each request and reads each response
choices.why: Right: OkHttp then sends the bytes.

choices.text: The database tables for the sessions
choices.why: That is Room, lesson 15.

choices.text: The token the server expects
choices.why: The token comes from the app, through an interceptor.

prompt: The base URL is `https://api.example.com/v1/` and a function is annotated `@GET("/courses")`, with a leading slash. Which address is requested?
hint: A relative link starting with a slash.

choices.text: `https://api.example.com/v1/courses`
choices.why: That is what `courses` without the slash gives.

choices.text: `https://api.example.com/courses`
choices.why: Right: the leading slash throws away `v1/`, as in a browser.

choices.text: Retrofit refuses the annotation at build time
choices.why: It is valid; it just resolves to another address.

choices.text: `https://api.example.com/v1//courses`
choices.why: URLs are resolved, not concatenated.

prompt: Why does the lesson keep `SessionDto` separate from `StudySession`?

choices.text: Retrofit cannot return a class with a `LocalDate`
choices.why: A converter could handle it; lesson 14 does. The reason is independence.

choices.text: So each side changes alone
choices.why: Right: a renamed server field changes one class.

choices.text: Because `data class` cannot be `@Serializable`
choices.why: The DTOs are serializable data classes.

choices.text: To use less memory on the phone
choices.why: Two classes do not save memory; that is not the point.

prompt: What does `server.takeRequest()` give the test?
hint: The server side of the conversation.

choices.text: The parsed list of courses
choices.why: That is what the client returned; `takeRequest` is the other end.

choices.text: The request as it arrived: method, path, headers, body
choices.why: Right: so the request itself is held to the contract.

choices.text: The next response in the queue
choices.why: Responses are enqueued; requests are taken.

choices.text: A copy of the OkHttp client
choices.why: The server knows nothing about the client object.

prompt: The POST's answer had no `done` field, yet the test printed `done=false`. Where did the value come from?

choices.text: From the default `= false` in `SessionDto`
choices.why: Right: a missing field takes the declared default.

choices.text: The server added it on the way back
choices.why: The server sent exactly the enqueued body, without `done`.

choices.text: OkHttp fills missing booleans with false
choices.why: OkHttp moves bytes; it knows nothing of the JSON's fields.

choices.text: From `NewSessionDto`, which the request carried
choices.why: `NewSessionDto` has no `done` field at all.

prompt: The test checked that the request carried the header `Authorization: ___ test-token`.
hint: The scheme name before the token.

prompt: Match each situation to what `apiCall` returns.

pairs.left: the server answers 200 with a list

prompt: Why does `apiCall` catch `HttpException` and `IOException` but not `Exception`?

choices.text: Catching `Exception` is refused by the Kotlin compiler
choices.why: It compiles; it would just be wrong.

choices.text: So cancellation and real bugs pass through
choices.why: Right: a cancelled call must cancel, and a bug must crash where you see it.

choices.text: Because Retrofit only throws those two
choices.why: It can throw others, a bug among them, and those must not be hidden.

choices.text: To keep the response body for the screen
choices.why: `Refused` keeps only the code.

prompt: The planner shows "Something went wrong" for every failure. What has it thrown away?
hint: One is something to tell, one is something to try again.

choices.text: Nothing, since the student cannot fix either
choices.why: The student can wait for a connection, and cannot fix a refusal; the words should say which.

choices.text: The HTTP method of the failed request
choices.why: The method matters to retries, not to the message.

choices.text: Whether to tell the student or to try again
choices.why: Right: refused and unreachable call for different actions.

choices.text: The token, which the error contains
choices.why: No error here carries the token.

prompt: In `ApiResultTest.noAnswer`, how many attempts did the server count before the call became `Unreachable`?
Which OkHttp timeout bounds the whole call, retries included?

choices.text: `readTimeout`
choices.why: It limits the wait between two pieces of the response.

choices.text: `connectTimeout`
choices.why: It limits opening a connection.

choices.text: `callTimeout`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `writeTimeout`
choices.why: It limits the wait between two pieces of the request.

prompt: A server sends one byte every nine seconds for two minutes. With only `readTimeout` at 10 s, what happens?
hint: Between two pieces, not the whole.

choices.text: It times out after ten seconds
choices.why: No gap reaches ten seconds, so it never trips.

choices.text: The student waits the full two minutes
choices.why: Right: only `callTimeout` bounds the whole call.

choices.text: OkHttp retries it three times
choices.why: Nothing failed, so nothing is retried.

choices.text: The connection is refused
choices.why: It was accepted; it is just slow.

prompt: A `POST` adding a session times out. Why does `RetryInterceptor` not send it again?
hint: What may have happened on the server?

choices.text: OkHttp forbids sending a body twice
choices.why: It allows it; the interceptor decides not to.

choices.text: It was perhaps saved, and only the answer lost
choices.why: Right: a second send would save it twice.

choices.text: A `POST` cannot time out
choices.why: Any call can time out.

choices.text: Because the token expires after one attempt
choices.why: The token is reused; that is not the reason.

prompt: A `GET` loses its connection twice and then succeeds. Put what `RetryInterceptor` does in order.
items: proceed a third time and return the response

prompt: In the `RetryTest` POST case, how many attempts reached the server?
hint: The printed line ends with it.

prompt: Why is the token passed to `AuthInterceptor` as a function and not a string?

choices.text: The token changes
choices.why: Right: each request reads the current one, or none.

choices.text: Because OkHttp requires every interceptor parameter to be a lambda
choices.why: OkHttp requires nothing of the constructor.

choices.text: To hide the token from the logging interceptor
choices.why: `redactHeader` does that.

choices.text: So the token is encrypted in memory
choices.why: A function encrypts nothing.

prompt: What did the log show for the `Authorization` header?

choices.text: Nothing: the line was removed
choices.why: The line is there, with its value hidden.

choices.text: `Bearer s3cr3t-t0ken`
choices.why: That would be the leak the lesson prevents.

choices.text: `Authorization: ██`
choices.why: Right: the header exists and its value does not reach the log.

choices.text: A hash of the token
choices.why: No hash is logged; the value is replaced.

prompt: Someone moves the logging interceptor before `AuthInterceptor`. What do the logs show from then on?
hint: Each interceptor sees the request after the ones to its left.

choices.text: Requests with no `Authorization` header
choices.why: Right: a log that lies about what was sent.

choices.text: The token in clear text
choices.why: The header does not exist yet at that point, redacted or not.

choices.text: Each request three times
choices.why: Retries happen after the logger, so it sees one call.

choices.text: Nothing changes
choices.why: Order changes what each interceptor sees.

prompt: Inside an interceptor, `chain.___(request)` passes the request on and returns the response.
hint: It appears in all three interceptors.

prompt: The planner's manifest never declared `INTERNET`, yet the merged manifest had it. Where did it come from?
hint: The merger report names the source.

choices.text: AGP adds it to every app
choices.why: The report named a library, not the plugin.

choices.text: `okhttp-android`'s own manifest
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Robolectric, for the tests
choices.why: Robolectric is a test dependency and never reaches the app's manifest.

choices.text: `targetSdk` 36 grants it implicitly
choices.why: No SDK level grants a permission by itself.

prompt: Why does the lesson put the cleartext exception in `src/debug/`?

choices.text: Because `res/xml` is only allowed in debug
choices.why: Any source set may have `res/xml`.

choices.text: It stays out of release builds
choices.why: Right: only the debug build merges it.

choices.text: Because the emulator only runs debug builds
choices.why: An emulator runs any build.

choices.text: To make the release APK smaller
choices.why: A small XML file is not about size.

prompt: What does `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` allow that the lesson's network security configuration does not?

choices.text: Plain HTTP to every address, in release builds too
choices.why: Right: the configuration names one address, in debug only.

choices.text: HTTPS to the emulator's host
choices.why: HTTPS was never blocked.

choices.text: Requests without the `INTERNET` permission
choices.why: Nothing removes the need for `INTERNET`.

choices.text: Nothing more: they are equivalent
choices.why: The attribute is far broader.

prompt: Which of these requests may `RetryInterceptor` send a second time? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `GET courses` whose connection dropped
choices.why: Yes: a GET after an `IOException`.

choices.text: `GET courses/chemistry/sessions` answered with 404
choices.why: No: an answer is not retried.

choices.text: `POST courses/android/sessions` that timed out
choices.why: No: a write is never repeated.

choices.text: `GET courses` that timed out on reading
choices.why: Yes: `SocketTimeoutException` is an `IOException`.

prompt: A test checks only `assertEquals(3, courses.size)`. Which bug does it miss that `takeRequest()` would catch?
hint: MockWebServer answers whatever path is asked.

choices.text: A wrong path, such as `/v1/course`
choices.why: Right: the queued answer comes back whatever the path.

choices.text: A wrong number of courses in the JSON
choices.why: The size assertion catches that.

choices.text: A course name with an accent
choices.why: Neither check is about names.

choices.text: A server slower than ten seconds
choices.why: That fails with a timeout either way.
